chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said:
I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the nosebleed: Does it break the wudu? He (peace be upon him) said: Only three things break the wudu: urine, faeces, and wind.
ai.seo_question: What are the three things that break wudu according to Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) clarifies the juristic status of a nosebleed (*al-nasur*) regarding ritual purity, establishing it as a non-invalidator of *wudu*. By explicitly limiting the invalidators to urine, feces, and wind, the Imam provides a precise textual basis for Shia fiqh, distinguishing minor impurities from those that necessitate a full renewal of ablution. This ruling underscores the principle of continuity of purity (*istishab*) unless a specific, proven cause for invalidation is present.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad,f rom Muhammad Bin Sahl, from Zakariyya Bin Adam who said,
‘I asked Al-Rezaasws about the nose bleed, ‘Does it break the Ablution (Wudhu)?’ Heasws said: ‘But rather, three things break the Ablution (Wudhu) – the urine, and the faeces, and the wind’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sahl from Zakariya ibn Adam who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, al-Rida, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a fistula (a bad wound) if it invalidates Wudu’ or not.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Only three things invalidate Wudu’: urine, feces and gas.’”
